name: rfc
description: Open and maintain a request for comment under docs/rfcs/: the options for a decision that has not been made, what each implies short, medium and long term, and a recommendation with a confidence score. An RFC precedes an ADR but is not required for one. Actions: list shows every RFC with its real status and the next free number; search {query} covers the RFCs and the ADRs together, so a decision already recorded surfaces before it is re-litigated; checklist {topic?} returns what an RFC has to pin down (the decision as a question, why now, disqualifying constraints, the status quo, scope, reversibility, who decides) with the question to put to the operator for each — use it with ask_user when the request is too vague to draft from, rather than inventing a scope. create {title, overview, slug?, research?} allocates the number, renders docs/rfcs/TEMPLATE.md and indexes it; passing a docs/research/ note links it and lifts its option headings in as stubs marked unverified, which are claims to re-check against their own sources, never content to keep. open, append, update maintain the body; recommend {path, recommendation, confidence 0-10, rationale, moves_confidence?, reversibility?} writes the Recommendation section; status {path, status, note?} moves it between draft, discussion, decided, deferred, withdrawn and superseded. An RFC needs real options: at least two candidates, the status quo, and one out-of-the-box possibility. Research the technical ones (the research tool's sweep, then web_fetch); for a direction question with nothing to search, find alternative perspectives and the strongest case against your own recommendation instead. rename moves an RFC to a new filename, rewrites its inventory link, and lists RFCs still naming the old one; the RFC keeps its number.
llm_description: Requests for comment under docs/rfcs/ — options, short/medium/long-term implications, and a recommendation with confidence 0-10. {action:"list"} shows status and the next number; {action:"search",query} covers RFCs and ADRs (a matching ADR may mean it is already decided); {action:"checklist",topic?} gives what to pin down and the question to ask the operator via ask_user when the request is vague. {action:"create",title,overview,slug?,research?} numbers, renders and indexes it; a research path is linked and its options seeded as UNVERIFIED stubs to re-check, not content. Then open/append/update, {action:"recommend",path,recommendation,confidence,rationale,moves_confidence?,reversibility?}, {action:"status",path,status:"draft"|"discussion"|"decided"|"deferred"|"withdrawn"|"superseded",note?}. Options must include the status quo and one out-of-the-box candidate; verify claims (research sweep, web_fetch) before they go in. Mutations are compare-and-swap — re-open after a conflict. {action:"rename",path,slug} moves an RFC to a new filename and rewrites its inventory link; pass the new name without a number -- an RFC's number is its identity and is not renamable, and citations written as "RFC 0022" are never found by the filename scan the reply lists.
prompt_guidance: A claim in an RFC is verified only by opening its ORIGINAL source in this same run — the exact URL, repository, or local file the claim comes from — with web_fetch, gh_read, read_file, or repo_search. A docs/research/ note is never a source: it is an earlier pass's summary, and re-reading it verifies nothing. Before a claim from a research note goes into an RFC body or recommendation, open the source the note cites for it; if you cannot open that source, write the claim as unverified. A claim the note itself marks low-confidence or unverified stays marked unverified until its origin is reopened. Before recommend, sweep the whole RFC: every load-bearing number, limit, licence, version, and maturity claim either names the source you reopened and the date, or says unverified.

action.description: list is the default; checklist before drafting a vague request; create scaffolds a numbered RFC. rename moves an RFC to a new filename, keeping its number.

topic.description: The subject of the decision, for checklist.

title.description: Title naming the decision, e.g. 'HTTP client for the proxy'. Required for create.

overview.description: What has to be decided and why now. Required for create; run checklist first when the request does not say.

slug.description: Filename stem after the number: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Derived from the title when omitted for create; for rename it is the new name only -- the record keeps its number, which is not renamable.

research.description: Optional path of a docs/research/ note to link and seed option stubs from. The stubs are unverified claims to re-check, not content.

path.description: Markdown path directly below docs/rfcs/. Required for open, append, update, recommend, and status.

content.description: Markdown to append to an existing RFC. Required for append. A block whose first line is a heading the record already carries with an empty body fills that section in place instead of adding a second copy of the heading.

old.description: Exact, uniquely occurring current text to replace. Required for update; obtain it with open.

new.description: Replacement text for update. May be empty to remove old text.

recommendation.description: The recommended option, or a phased path. Required for recommend.

confidence.description: Confidence in the recommendation, 0 to 10. Required for recommend. Four or below means the evidence is not there yet.

rationale.description: Why this beats the runner-up against the stated constraints. Required for recommend.

moves_confidence.description: What evidence would raise the confidence, and what finding would sink the recommendation.

reversibility.description: How hard the decision is to undo, and where the point of no return is.

status.description: New status. Required for status; decided and superseded also need a note.

note.description: Sentence appended to the status line: the ADR that records a decision, or what supersedes this RFC.

query.description: Text to search for across the RFCs and ADRs. Required for search.
